vectors.name: schema-wellformedness/refs/dangling-reference-is-an-error
vectors.comment: S-6: a Ref MUST resolve to a name present in env. `Ghost` is not a scalar keyword, not `any`, and not a defined record, so it is a dangling reference.

vectors.name: schema-wellformedness/root/root-name-not-defined-is-an-error
vectors.comment: S-1: the root MUST be a Ref that resolves in env. `Ghost` is never defined, so the schema's own entry point is dangling -- the same failure mode as S-6 applied to the root position specifically. Path is $ (no specific record to name, same fallback reasoning as osd-grammar/root/missing-root-is-an-error) since Ghost is the undefined name, not a record that exists to be blamed.

vectors.name: schema-wellformedness/refs/forward-reference-is-legal
vectors.comment: S-6: forward references are explicitly legal. `R` refers to `Later`, which is declared after it -- declaration order does not constrain reference resolution.

vectors.name: schema-wellformedness/refs/mutual-recursion-is-legal
vectors.comment: S-6: mutual recursion is explicitly legal (env is finite, so every operation in ch.6 still terminates despite the cycle). Both fields are optional, since an all-mandatory mutual cycle would make the schema unsatisfiable (ch.6 Sec6.4) -- a well-formedness question, not this vector's concern.
